To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the formation of adult muscles during metamorphosis is controlled by the sequential expression of three genes, each encoding a transcription factor.

imaginal myogenesis in D. melanogaster is a complex developmental process involving a diverse set of muscle progenitor cells and a large repertoire of myogenic transcription factors and signalling molecules.

the genetic and molecular mechanisms of imaginal muscle development in Drosophala are conserved with those of vertebrate muscle development, and that imaginal muscles are derived from a common progenitor pool of muscle precursor cells that are specified by Notch signalling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how a relatively simple genetic programme can generate such a diverse pattern of myogenesis.
understanding the mechanisms that generate a diverse pattern of muscles in Drosophia and the role that this pattern plays in the development of the behavioural repertoire of the adult fly.
understanding how a complex pattern of muscle fibbers is formed in Drosophia, and how this pattern is controlled by genetic and molecular mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the molecular and genetic mechanisms of imaginal myoblast specification and myotube formation in Drosophilia are not well understood.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of imaginal myoblast fusion and myofibre assembly have yet to be determined.
we are still in the early stages of understanding how imaginal muscle development is patterned.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic and molecular control of imaginal muscle pattern diversification has been elucidated to an extent that is unprecedented for any animal.
, in the adult fly, the genetic and molecular control of muscle development is highly complex and involves a large array of genes and regulatory mechanisms that are only beginning to be unravelled.
, in Drosophala, imaginal myogenesis is a complex and highly regulated process that involves a diverse array of genes and signalling pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the genetic and molecular mechanisms of muscle development are remarkably similar between vertebrates and invertebrates, and that many of the same molecules are involved in both embryonic and imaginal muscle formation.
the mechanisms of muscle pattern formation are surprisingly conserved between Drosophila imaginal myogenesis and vertebrate limb muscle development.

, in the absence of any obvious patterning cues, imaginal myogenesis is driven by a small number of conserved transcriptional regulators that act in a combinatorial fashion to define muscle identity and position.
